answer: Under standard plans, you must submit a reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. (An archived 2024 rule previously specified a 15-day deadline [3]).
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4]. If you occupy a room exceeding this limit, proportionate deduction applies to all associated hospital charges [5].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard/retail plans, unless explicitly waived in writing by Aurora [3][5]. Under the Aurora Senior Care plan, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].
As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

The no-claim bonus for Aurora Gold is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. A claim does not reduce the accumulated bonus; it only stops accumulation for that specific year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If Aurora's final internal response is unsatisfactory, you may escalate the matter to the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1]. You can also approach the Insurance Ombudsman if Aurora has not responded within 30 days of the original complaint [1].

Across all plans, there is road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan covers air ambulance up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, but there is no separate waiting period [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. It lasts 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. During this time, a new policyholder may cancel and receive a refund of the premium minus proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You get 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment does not qualify as a day-care procedure [3].
For an emergency admission under cashless, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid. Under Silver with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, your room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because you chose a room at ₹15,000 per day, an eligibility ratio of 0.667 applies, resulting in proportionate deductions on room rent and associated medical expenses [1][5].

The Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans allow you to add dependent parents, though the Silver plan requires an extra premium to do so [1]. Adding your mother will affect your premium because policy premiums are determined by the age of the eldest covered member [4].

Credit for the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy (including its accrued no-claim bonus) [1][2]. Any incremental or increased sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods [1][2].

To continue coverage for your newborn beyond the first 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the baby to your policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. Doing so within this 90-day window guarantees coverage without medical underwriting, whereas waiting until after will result in the child being treated as a fresh applicant [1]. If you need to submit a reimbursement claim for the hospital delivery, that claim must be submitted within 30 days of discharge [3].

On the Silver plan, having a claim reduces your accumulated bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset your bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the coverage limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, your out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

No, knee replacement is not covered immediately unless it is required following an accident [1][5]. Otherwise, knee joint replacement is subject to a 24-month waiting period from policy commencement [1][3][5]. Claims resulting from accidental injury are covered immediately from day one [2][5].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium, but the wellness discount—which can be up to 15%—is applied last after the cap and is the only discount permitted to exceed it [1][3][5]. Consequently, the total maximum discount achievable is 45% of the base premium (a 30% capped discount plus up to a 15% wellness discount) [1][3][5].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider [3][4]. Your only option is to seek payment through reimbursement [1][3][5]. However, a claim from an excluded provider is only payable on reimbursement if the admission was a genuine emergency, no alternative facility was reachable, and pre-approval is required [1][3].

The deadline depends on the type of claim:

* For motor insurance claims, you have 30 days from the date of the query to respond [4].
* For general/reimbursement claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond, after which Aurora closes the claim [2][5].

According to current guidelines, a planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3]. However, an archived 2024 timeline states the deadline is 48 hours before admission [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If a query is raised, the clock restarts once the queried document is supplied [1]. (Note that an archived 2024 policy previously specified a 30-day timeline [3].)
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at all ages [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Silver plan has no co-payment when the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

Across the four plans, the pre-hospitalisation cover windows are 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. The corresponding post-hospitalisation cover windows across the four plans are 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days [1].

To have cover for dependent parents-in-law, you must choose either the Gold or Platinum plan [1]. Among these, the Gold plan removes room-rent sub-limits [3]. The provided sources do not specify whether the Platinum plan has a room-rent sub-limit.

Under permanent exclusions, dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Out-patient dental work is also noted as an item not covered by any plan [1].
